calls.head: McKenna’s line gets the soft minutes
calls.body: At home, the Maple Leafs keep sending McKenna’s line (McKenna, Paul and Joshua) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jim Hiller has been chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Wild’s fourth line is M. Foligno, Hartman and N. Foligno.
calls.call: The Maple Leafs’ L3 (McKenna, Paul and Joshua) spends at least 24% of its 5-on-5 time against the Wild’s fourth line, against about 14% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 34% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against fourth lines, about 14% with no line matching

chips.tip: Toronto’s L3 (McKenna, Paul and Joshua) at home: 34% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ fourth lines. Matchups, Toronto home games this season, 12 games, 45 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face fourth lines about 14% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

calls.happened: Toronto’s L3 (McKenna, Paul, Joshua) spent 5% of its 5-on-5 time against Minnesota’s L4 (0:26 of 8:32). The call needed 24%, halfway from the 14% it would get with no line matching to its home habit of 34%.

lane.tip: Share of this group’s 5-on-5 time against that line tonight (the filled dot). The ring is the call: halfway from what it would get with no line matching (the tick) to its home habit (the dotted mark), since part of any habit is luck. Reaching the ring holds the call; past the tick is partly; otherwise it didn’t happen.

calls.title: McKenna, Paul and Joshua barely saw the Wild’s fourth line
calls.plain: Toronto sent McKenna, Paul and Joshua out against the Wild’s fourth line no more than they would with no line matching. Instead, Hiller sent them out against Shabanov, Yurov and Trenin (4:25 of 8:32 at 5-on-5).
calls.said: Jim Hiller would send McKenna, Paul and Joshua out against the Wild’s fourth line again

calls.head: Tilted ice, toward the Maple Leafs’ net
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Wild have been near the top of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Maple Leafs one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Wild’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

surprises.head: Minnesota shut down Toronto’s power play
surprises.body: Toronto has a better power play than most. Not tonight: 1.7 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 8.3 and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

story.head: Boldy bags a hat trick
paras: Matt Boldy got the scoring started for the Wild late in the first. Auston Matthews and Zack MacEwen scored just under three minutes apart early in the second to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. The Wild’s Joel Eriksson Ek left in the second period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with an upper-body injury. Boldy scored again on the power play midway through the period to tie it 2-2, and he completed his hat trick early in the third to put the Wild ahead 3-2. Michael McCarron made it 4-2 three and a half minutes later. Danila Yurov added an empty-net goal with just under a minute left to make it 5-2. Kirill Kaprizov finished with three assists.

The chances were closer than the score. Wallstedt shook off a shaky start for the Wild, allowing two goals on the first eight shots and none on the last 20, and Anthony Stolarz stopped 21 of 25 at the other end. Wallstedt has won five straight starts. The Wild moved to 14-3-4, tied for first in the NHL in points, while the Maple Leafs dropped to 8-11-2, seventh in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Wild have points in ten straight games (8-0-2).
Matt Boldy passed Pierre-Marc Bouchard for ninth on the Wild’s all-time scoring list, with 350 points.
The Maple Leafs are on a five-game losing streak.
Kirill Kaprizov has a point in ten straight games.
